headlines.article_text: Stock market today: Live updates Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Traders work on the floor at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) in New York City, US, Nov. 18, 2026. Brendan McDermid | Reuters U.S. equity futures jumped early Thursday as investors looked ahead to Anthropic's public trading debut. Futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.38%. S&P 500 futures added 0.59%, and Nasdaq-100 futures surged 0.99% In Asia, markets were mostly lower. South Korea's Kospi fell 0.25% as markets opened an hour later than usual due to the country's annual college entrance exam . Hong Kong's Hang Seng index fell 1.89%, while mainland China's CSI 300 declined 0.49%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 closed 1.08% lower. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 0.48%, while the Topix fell 0.15%. In Wednesday's regular U.S. trading, the blue-chip Dow lost more than 560 points, or 1.1%. The broad market S&P 500 fell 0.2%, marking its fifth consecutive losing session and longest slide since June. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4%. Traders are focused on how the company behind Claude performs when it debuts on the Nasdaq Thursday, trading under the ticker "ANT." The artificial intelligence company priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above the expected range, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC Wednesday. Anthropic also upsized the offering, selling around 980 million shares, bringing the amount raised to $81.3 billion and surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June. The market has become more cautious on AI as of late, with investors focusing on whether heavy spending on the build-out will translate into meaningful profits. The iShares AI Innovation and Tech Active ETF (BAI) has fallen 11% this month, and embattled AI bellwether Nvidia has dropped 26% while the company grapples with the resignation of its CEO Jensen Huang. Shares of neocloud CoreWeave , which had seen its bond yields trade above 16% earlier this month, is also down almost 13% in November alone. "It'll be an important barometer for investors' AI appetite," Callie Cox, director of investment strategy at Plancorp, said of Anthropic's IPO. "AI stocks desperately need some wind at their backs, too ... Wall Street needs a sign that investors still believe in the potential for AI beyond already-elevated expectations." "The challenge in that thesis is that hot IPOs rarely perform well right out of the gate, especially these days, when every company seems to be vying for a limited pool of capital to fund their AI strategy," she said. "While I wouldn't be surprised to see the stock market take cues from Anthropic's performance, I'd caution investors about trying to read the tea leaves from one event too much." On Thursday, traders will keep an eye out for weekly jobless claims. On the earnings front, Walmart is slated to report in the morning, followed by clothing retailer Gap after the market close.

headlines.article_text: Musk says Jensen Huang is irreplaceable, regrets midterm spending Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Elon Musk said at the NYT DealBook Summit that ousting Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO did not seem like a "smart decision." Musk added he felt "pretty foolish" about spending at least $474 million on the U.S. midterms. On a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger, Musk said areas of overlap between the companies now exist that "didn't exist before." In this article NVDA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT (L-R) Andrew Ross Sorkin and Elon Musk speak during the NY Times Dealbook Summit at Jazz at Lincoln Center, Nov. 18, 2026 in New York City. Adam Gray | Getty Images Elon Musk compared Jensen Huang 's departure from Nvidia to kicking Michael Jordan off a team on a winning streak, while also expressing regret over how much he spent on the U.S. midterms. "You've got a winning streak ... and then you kick Michael Jordan off your team," Musk told Andrew Ross Sorkin at The New York Times' DealBook Summit on Wednesday. He added, "Doesn't seem like a smart decision to me." watch now VIDEO 1:25 01:25 Elon Musk: Everyone I know thinks Jensen Huang should have stayed on as Nvidia CEO News Videos Huang resigned last week following pressure after disclosing an affair with a woman who reportedly was suspected of being a Chinese spy, alongside reports of relationships with employees. He is expected to testify before the U.S. Congress next month around national-security and export-control issues. The SpaceX and Tesla chief executive, who previously said it would be an "honor" to hire the Nvidia co-founder, added that no one could really replace Huang. Musk said he had heard similar views about Huang's departure from Nvidia, including from President Donald Trump . "I think the president has voiced publicly that he thinks Jensen should have stayed as CEO, and everyone I know thinks the same ... this is, at the end of the day, the Nvidia board decision," he said, adding, "We're not on the board, right?" Musk and Huang have known each other for years through Nvidia's work with Tesla and OpenAI. Tesla has been a major Nvidia customer, while Huang has repeatedly praised Musk's AI strategy, including Tesla's self-driving work, xAI and the Optimus robot. Midterms, Tesla and SpaceX Asked about the midterms, Musk said he felt "pretty foolish" about spending at least $474 million with little to show for it, though he added that "maybe it would have been much worse without that." Musk said his goal had been to prevent the presidency, House and Senate from all being controlled by one party. "If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money," he said. watch now VIDEO 2:43 02:43 Elon Musk: If I could rewind the clock, I would have spent less money on U.S. midterms News Videos In the same interview, he also appeared to distance himself from the MAGA movement. "I'm not MAGA," he said, adding that he wasn't sure what the term means. On a possible SpaceX-Tesla merger, Musk said areas of overlap now exist that "didn't exist before," pointing to AI, robotics and the AI software and chip-design teams at both companies. He said any deal would require shareholder approval and "may or may not succeed." Musk added that he could not push through a transaction that was bad for shareholders because he would "obviously get sued." Asked whether he should receive his Tesla pay award if a merger were completed, Musk said he should not be rewarded "just for doing a merger" and should receive stock-option awards only if Tesla meets its performance targets. Musk also said SpaceX rents computing capacity to Anthropic under short-term agreements that either side can terminate, adding that the Claude AI chatbot-maker had expressed interest in an additional 10 gigawatts. watch now VIDEO 2:28 02:28 Elon Musk: More areas of overlap between SpaceX and Tesla than before News Videos Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 per share on Wednesday, raising $81.3 billion in what it said was the largest public offering on record, surpassing SpaceX. Asked how he feels a year after describing his mind as "a storm," Musk said he feels "relatively at peace."
